cases.surface_condition: the token immediately AFTER the marker is an ordinal or numeric ordinal word (e.g. "fifteenth", "ninth", "1st") and the LEFT ends in a finite verb
cases.blamed_rule: Arly <SEG:5> Velasquez <SEG:20> finished <SEG:70> fifteenth <SEG:35> in <SEG:2> the Paralympics slalom event.
cases.proposed_rule: If the immediate right token is an ordinal/cardinal numeral or ordinal adjective (1st/2nd/"first","fifteenth", etc.) AND the left-most side ends with a finite verb, treat the right as a likely verb complement and force the score down into 0–20.

cases.surface_condition: the right begins with existential 'there' followed immediately by a finite verb ("there is/are/was/were ...")
cases.proposed_rule: If the immediate right token is the existential 'there' and it is followed within 1–2 tokens by a finite verb, treat the cut as a clause-continuation risk and lower the score into the 41–60 band (good-but-risky) instead of scoring it very high.

cases.surface_condition: the right begins with a copular/copula or other finite verb ("is/are/was/were") while the left is a bare NP (no finite verb immediately before)
cases.blamed_rule: Surface signals: left ends in what looks like a clause but either (a) the right begins with a verb that lacks an explicit subject (verb continuing from left), or (b) the right begins with a subordinating/continuation signal (but, although, where) or a prepositional head (of, to, in) suggesting continuation.
cases.proposed_rule: Sharpen the existing 41–60 rule: require a stronger downward move when the right token is a copula/finite verb (is/are/was/were) and the left lacks a finite verb — set such cuts to 21–40 (weak cut) because the right is likely the predicate of the left NP.

calibration_fix: Lower the example anchor that encourages high scores after verbs: change the example output 'finished <SEG:70>' in the Arly example to something like 'finished <SEG:20>'.
summary: The prompt systematically overweights left-side completeness (finite verbs and punctuation anchors, and some example anchors) and under-recognises right-headed continuations that function as verb complements or predicates. Add explicit patterns for ordinals/numerals, existential 'there', and copular/finites starting the right side (and sharpen the copula rule already present) so these cuts are pushed into lower bands. Also re-anchor the illustrative example that currently teaches high scores after verbs to correct calibration.
